expected.rationale: the application loads this package on the firing signal, so it really is in use. The expected verdict is what the first stage's rules alone produce. A module loaded this way is read and closed, so it appears neither in the process's open descriptors nor in its mapped files: this package is expected to be reachable only through an event record, which is the point of the case

fixture_notes.vulnerable_package_selection: lodash 4.17.15, verified against this image with the scanner used here: four HIGH findings (CVE-2020-8203, CVE-2021-23337, CVE-2026-4800, NSWG-ECO-516), all attributed to app/node_modules/lodash/package.json. Chosen because it is a plain library with no service or network requirement, so loading it is the only thing the run does
fixture_notes.layout: the standard package manager's layout, with the real package directly under the application's module directory
fixture_notes.other_packages_present: the runtime image also carries the package manager's own dependencies under a separate module directory. Those are not loaded by this application, and whether an observation distinguishes them from the application's own dependency is part of what the case measures
fixture_notes.system_call_level_truth: none; the system-call capture rate is reported as unavailable
fixture_notes.timestamp_precision: the timestamps are a wall-clock reading to the millisecond with a sub-millisecond part taken from a different clock. The two are not the same clock, so the digits below a millisecond are not a measurement of anything: treat the resolution as one millisecond, and keep the pairing tolerance well above it
